methods.label: Separate positive and negative denominators
methods.explanation:
The reciprocal requires \(x\ne0\). Before multiplying an inequality by \(x\), separate its possible signs, because a negative multiplier reverses the inequality.

If \(x>0\), then \(1/x>0>-3\), so the lower bound is automatic. The remaining inequality gives
\[
\frac1x<2\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad1<2x
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x>\frac12.
\]
If \(x<0\), then \(1/x<0<2\), so the upper bound is automatic. Multiplying the lower bound by the negative number \(x\) reverses its direction:
\[
\frac1x>-3\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad1<-3x
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x<-\frac13.
\]
These cases cover every nonzero real \(x\). The endpoints give equality in one original bound and are excluded. Thus the solution is \(\boxed{x>\frac12\text{ or }x<-\frac13}\), choice E.
